“The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook,” but the Committee’s simultaneous move to the zero lower bound, large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, and liquidity backstops (discount window, repo, and dollar swap lines) should materially cushion the downturn by easing credit frictions and supporting aggregate demand—consistent with the credit channel literature (Bernanke and Gertler; Gertler and Gilchrist; Oliner and Rudebusch) and with research showing that credible, forward-looking monetary policy can stabilize expectations around the inflation target (Svensson; Walsh). With market-based inflation compensation falling but survey expectations little changed, anchoring at the symmetric 2 percent objective also reduces real-rate pressures in a liquidity-stressed environment, mitigating deflation risks. Net tone: still negative given the shock, but less so once policy mitigation is incorporated.
